message.content:
Below is a ready‑to‑run **gcloud** command (the official CLI for Google Cloud) that creates a Compute Engine VM with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
If you prefer the raw REST/JSON payload you’ll find that next.

---

### 1️⃣ Create the instance with `gcloud`

```bash
# 1. Set your project and zone (replace PROJECT_ID & ZONE)
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# 2. Create a new VM named “rtx-a6000-demo” with:
#    • Machine type: n1-standard‑8 (8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM – adjust if needed)
#    • Boot disk: Ubuntu 20.04 LTS (latest LTS image)
#    • One NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU
#    • Preemptible (optional but cheaper) – remove --preemptible if you want a regular instance
#    • Allow SSH via metadata key (you can add your public key here)

gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-demo \
  --project=$PROJECT_ID \
  --zone=$ZONE \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
  --boot-disk-size=200GB \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --metadata-from-file ssh-keys=~/.ssh/google_compute_engine.pub \
  --accelerator=count=1,type=nvidia-tesla-a6000 \
  --guest-os-features=GPU_TESLA \
  --no-shielded-secure-boot \
  --no-shielded-vtpm \
  --no-shielded-integrity-monitoring \
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --network-interface=network-tier=PREMIUM,subnet=default \
  --reservation-affinity=any
```

> **Notes**
> * Replace `PROJECT_ID` and `ZONE` with your own values.
> * Adjust `--machine-type` if you need more or fewer CPUs/RAM.
> * The `--metadata-from-file ssh-keys` line injects your public SSH key so you can log in immediately.
> * The `--guest-os-features=GPU_TESLA` flag tells GCP to install the NVIDIA driver automatically after the first boot.

After running the command, you’ll see output similar to:

```
Creating [instance rtx-a6000-demo]…done.
Created [instance rtx-a6000-demo].
```

You can then SSH into the machine:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-demo --project=$PROJECT_ID --zone=$ZONE
```

Once logged in, the NVIDIA drivers will be installed automatically (you might need to reboot). Verify the GPU:

```bash
nvidia-smi
```

---

### 2️⃣ Equivalent REST API call (JSON body)

If you’re calling the Compute Engine REST API directly (e.g., from a script or Terraform), the request body would look like this:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-demo",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 200
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [{ "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      { "key": "ssh-keys", "value": "$(cat ~/.ssh/google_compute_engine.pub)" }
    ]
  },
  "tags": { "items": ["http-server", "https-server"] },
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "shieldedInstanceConfig": {
    "enableSecureBoot": false,
    "enableVtpm": false,
    "enableIntegrityMonitoring": false
  }
}
```

Send this JSON to the endpoint:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_OAUTH_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json
Body: <above JSON>
```

Replace `{PROJECT_ID}` and `{ZONE}` with your actual values. After the POST succeeds, the instance will be created exactly as described above.

---

#### Quick checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|---|------|
| ✅ | Project ID set |
| ✅ | Zone selected |
| ✅ | Machine type chosen |
| ✅ | Disk size & OS family set |
| ✅ | GPU type (`nvidia-tesla-a6000`) added |
| ✅ | Metadata includes your SSH key |
| ✅ | Guest OS features flag set (`GPU_TESLA`) |

That’s all you need! Once the instance boots, the NVIDIA driver will auto‑install, and you’ll have a fully functional RTX A6000 GPU ready for CUDA workloads.
